newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: RESCUERS UNABLE TO REACH COLLAPSED SKI LODGES
In the New South Wales Snowy Mountains, rescue authorities still have not been able to reach two collapsed ski lodges, buried under a landslide at the Thredbo ski village.
Up to 20 people are missing, feared dead, under tonnes of rubble.
The landslide occured just before midnight last night causing the Carinya ski lodge to collapse onto the Bimbadeen staff lodge.
Eighteen to 20 people are unaccounted for.
Initial rescue attempts by local police were abandoned due to the unstable surrounding landscape.
Large cranes are now being used in an attempt to clear some of the debris.
Rescue efforts are being co-ordinated under the Snowy River disaster plan.
More than 100 emergency personnel have headed to the area. Other specialists are on their way.
A geo-physicist is helping police assess rescue options and a soil scientist from Sydney is also bring brought in.
Engineers from the Snowy Mountains Engineering Corporation have been alerted and mines rescue personnel from the Illwarra are being flown in by navy helicopters.
Concerned relatives have been asked to call a special hotline, 1800 227228, rather than local police.
SINGAPORE MINISTER SAYS HANSON DEBATE NEEDED
A senior Asian politician says Australia should continue with its internal questioning of its place in Asia and the issue of immigration.
Singapore's Information Minister and Junior Minister for Trade and Industry, Brigadier-General George Yeo, says he's suprised the debate didn't arise some years ago.
The Minister made his comments following the launch of a new program to attract Australian students to Singapore which he says will strengthen ties between the two countries.
Mr Yeo says if managed well the debate prompted by Pauline Hanson can lead to a healthy outcome.
"Because you have to focus minds on the important issues. And adjustments can be made. And in the end Australian society must make certain choices," Mr Yeo said.
"I mean you want to be part of Asia but you do not want to lose your past, which I think is very legitimate desire," he said.
CHILD DIABETES LEAPS
A leading specialist says there has been an unexpected leap in the number of children contracting Diabetes.
Researchers say they are unsure what is causing the increase.
The Director of the New Childrens Hospital's Diabetes Unit, Dr Neville Howard, says the latest statistics show a rise of 30 percent in the incidence of Childhhod Diabetes in New South Wales.
He warned the figure only represents newly diagnosed cases and the prevelance of the disease will, in fact, be much higher.
Dr Howard called for urgent research into the problem and for improved techniques to help avoid long term complications such as blindness and kidney diseases.
Dr Howard says the rise can't be explained by genetic factors.
He says the only feasible explanation is a yet-to-be determined environmental cause.
Meanwhile, a new study shows a link between diabetes and binge eating in younger women.

Queensland University Clinical psychologist, Dr Justin Kenardy's study of 200 women at the Diabetic Education Centre in Newcastle found one third suffered from a binge eating disorder and had type two, or non insuline-dependent diabetes.
Typically type two diabetes sufferers are older and need a strict diet to keep the disease in check.
Dr Kenardy says binge eating could be a catalyst to diabetes.
MANDELA WELCOMES RELEASE OF TIMOR ACTIVIST
South African President Nelson Mandela says the release of jailed Timorese activist Xanana Gusmao is crucial to finding a lasting settlement to the dispute over Timorese sovereignty.
President Mandela has emerged as a crucial figure in renewed efforts to broker an agreement on the issue.
Mr Mandela has held talks with the Presidents of Indonesia and Portugal as well as Timorese resistance leaders in an attempt to resolve the dispute over East Timor.

He's urging Indonesia's President Suharto to release jailed activist Xanana Gusmao, warning the situation in East Timor can never be normalised until all political leaders have been released from prison.
President Mandela's involvement brings renewed impetus to negotiations and he says he believes his appeal has received a sympathic hearing.

Speaking after talks with the Portuguese leader in Pretoria, President Mandela said he will now pursue further meetings with Timorese leaders, saying anything he does must be consistent with their ideas.
However, he has refused to release further details of his peace initiative.
TELSTRA GRANTS LICENCES FOR ELECTRONIC BILLING
Telstra has granted the first of what it hopes will be a number of international licences, to use its new electronic billing system, called Flexcab.
The carrier has just signed a multi-million dollar deal with Telecom Argentina.
Combined with two other agreements, expected with American telecommunications companies, the system is tipped to generate up to $75-million in export earnings.
A spokesperson says around 350 jobs should be created at Telstra's skills transfer centre in Melbourne, training overseas computer programmers to use Flexcab.
She says Telstra will retain intellectual property rights over the system.
BREAKTHROUGH FOR THOSE LOOKING TO ADOPT CHILD FROM OVERSEAS
There is new hope for childless couples looking to adopt a child from overseas, following a meeting of the Community Services Ministerial Council in Cairns.
The Queensland Community Care Minister, Kev Lingard, says the States agreed to accept the Hague convention, which sets out rules and standards for adopting children from overseas countries.
Mr Lingard says it will make it easier for couples to adopt kids from overseas.
"Under under this particular program what it does is clear the way quickly for them to get into the procedures. I mean adoPting children from overseas is very time consuming", Mr Lingard said.
BORAL TALKS TO RESUME TOMORROW
Negotiations between union officials and management of the Boral timber company broke down this afternoon, with a view to call in Boral's senior management.
High level talks were being held in Sydney today to resolve a dispute over claims Boral had negotiated individual contracts with some staff, while collective agreements were in force.
The timber workers union, the CFMEU, had threatened rolling stoppages would be held from two o'clock today, if the dispute was not resolved.
But the union's Andrew Harden says the Australian manager of Boral will take part in talks tomorrow morning in a last minute attempt to end the dispute.
INTEREST RATE CUT TO BOOST BUILDING INDUSTRY: MBA
Today's half a per cent cut in official interest rates is expected to boost the building industry.
The Master Builders Association's Lachlan McDonald, said the early stages of recovery are underway in Victoria, with an increase in the number of private homes being constructed.
Mr McDonald said while it had been fairly patchy so far, there does seem to be some recovery in the state's building industry and these cuts in interest rates will help.
